Regression Trees and Interaction Detection

Motivation: Interactions

A linear model assumes additive effects

\[ Y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 X_1 + \beta_2 X_2 \]

But in many real situations we have interactions

\[ Y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 X_1 + \beta_2 X_2 + \beta_3 X_1X_2 \]

This means the effect of one variable depends on another.

Simulated Dataset with Interaction

  • Here the relationship between salary and experience changes depending on another variable (college degree).

  • We can use the classical linear model for this type of interactions.

Key Takeaways

Regression trees:

  • Automatically detect interactions
  • Handle nonlinear relationships
  • Partition the feature space
  • Produce interpretable rules

Trees were historically motivated by Automatic Interaction Detection (AID) in the 1960s.
